declared_proposition: Let Xi(z)=xi(1/2+i z), and let S_n be its Taylor sections at zero. On the closed first exhaustion rectangles D_2^+ and D_2^-, Xi has no zero. Consequently, for each sign there exists an index n for which S_n has zero count zero in D_2^sign and satisfies sup_boundary|Xi-S_n|<inf_boundary|S_n|. This is an existential actual-Xi Rouché theorem, not an explicit interval certificate.
mathematical_argument: For z=x+i y, s=1/2+i z=(1/2-y)+i x. The upper closed rectangle maps to -3/2<=Re(s)<=0 and the lower one to 1<=Re(s)<=5/2. Every zero of the completed xi function is a nontrivial zeta zero and therefore has 0<Re(s)<1; xi(0)=xi(1)=1/2. Hence Xi is zero-free on both compact closures. If delta is its positive minimum modulus there, uniform Taylor convergence gives sup|Xi-S_n|<delta/3. Then inf|S_n|>=2delta/3, and Rouché gives the asserted zero count and strict boundary inequality.

reproducible_computation.no_go_scope: D_2 avoids the open critical strip, so closing it is not evidence that controls an off-critical zero. The proof is existential and does not output a Taylor degree, coefficient enclosure, or margin.

remaining_gap: The first D_2 certificate is existential, has no explicit Taylor degree or interval margin, and avoids the open critical strip entirely.
claim_boundary: No RH proof or counterexample. The first actual-Xi rectangle is closed only existentially and lies outside the open critical strip.
